findings.title: Switching a variant's preorder off strands every unpaid or unresolved preorder order: the commit reads capacity that the form has just nulled
findings.evidence: finance.order_try_commit decides by the reservation's own flag: `if r.res_preorder then v_free := coalesce(r.preorder_capacity, 0) - finance.preorder_committed(r.variant_id) - ...` (lines 648-650), and the stock loop skips such lines (`not coalesce(x.preorder, false)`, line 676). The variant form nulls the capacity when the switch goes off (`preorder_capacity: preorder ? (values.preorder_capacity ?? null) : null`, src/admin/tables/variants.ts:97), so v_free becomes 0 - committed < quantity. order_resolve (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:963) calls the same function and answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE; nothing ever rewrites a reservation's preorder flag. docs/operations.md:1083-1089 tells the owner to switch preorder off when the copies arrive and says nothing about open holds. The rule is deliberate (P08-CONTRACT.md:173, 613-614) and pinned by tests/integration/payment.test.ts:1664-1673 (a reservation flagged preorder on a variant with null capacity -> paid_needs_resolution), but neither the contract, the test nor the runbook follows it to the switch-off moment, where every open preorder hold meets a null capacity.
findings.impact: Precondition: a buyer holds a preorder reservation (unpaid, inside the 20-minute hold, or an attempt paying) or an order sits in paid_needs_resolution at the moment the owner switches the preorder off, which is the planned lifecycle event. The buyer's payment then lands as paid_needs_resolution although the real stock is on the shelf, and the owner's «حلّ الطلب» answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE for ever; the only way out is a refund. Money is kept, so no loss, but a paid order the owner cannot deliver through the admin.
findings.proposed_fix: In finance.order_try_commit treat a preorder reservation on a variant that is no longer a preorder by the stock rule: compute `v_as_preorder := r.res_preorder and v.preorder` (join v.preorder into the loop) and use it both in the free check and in the stock-decrement loop's `not coalesce(x.preorder, false)` condition; alternatively refuse the switch-off (trigger on product_variants) while a held unexpired or uncommitted preorder reservation exists and say so in the form. payment.test.ts:1664 then asserts the new rule (commit by stock when the variant is no longer a preorder), not the old outcome.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack: make variant V a preorder (capacity 5, date tomorrow); checkout_create one line of V qty 1 (reservation preorder=true, held); as owner update product_variants set preorder=false, preorder_capacity=null, preorder_ships_on=null, preorder_note=null, stock=10 where id=V; then apply a verified paid payment for the attempt (emulator). Expect orders.status = 'paid_needs_resolution' and select public.order_resolve(order_id) -> {ok:false, code:'STOCK_UNAVAILABLE'} although stock = 10 and no other hold exists.

findings.title: A digital order line whose variant was later made physical is stock-checked and decrements stock at payment
findings.evidence: The commit loop joins the variant's CURRENT columns: `elsif r.stock is not null then v_free := r.stock - ...` (line 651-652) and the decrement loop `where ... v.stock is not null and not coalesce(x.preorder, false)` (line 676) never look at the item's snapshot `i.fulfillment` or at whether a reservation exists. A digital, non-preorder line has no reservation (checkout_create inserts one only `where l ->> 'fulfillment' <> 'digital' or ...preorder`, 20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:611). The owner may change `fulfillment` and `stock` through the Data API (`grant update (... fulfillment, ... stock ...)`, 20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:284).
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner turns a digital variant into a physical one (setting a stock) while an unpaid order with a digital line of it exists. That line is then refused for stock (paid_needs_resolution if stock < quantity) or, when stock suffices, one physical unit is decremented and audited for a copy that is delivered as a file (the entitlement is still created from the snapshot). Rare, bounded to one owner action, but it is a wrong stock state.
findings.proposed_fix: Restrict both loops to lines that hold a reservation (`join finance.inventory_reservations x` instead of `left join`, or `where x.id is not null`): a physical or signed line always has one, a digital preorder has one, a digital non-preorder line has none and needs no stock.

findings.title: commerce_policies_approve still reads the live policy seqs without any lock, so an approval that overlaps a publish records a seq that is already replaced and the reset trigger never fires
findings.evidence: The final body (audit2_fixes, the create or replace of 20260927170000_policy_approval.sql) does `select seq into v_store from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store';` four times with plain SELECTs (lines 112-115) after locking only finance.commerce_settings. The reset trigger `policies_reset_approval` (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:141-145) updates the settings row only `where policy_revisions ? v_doc`, so while the approval is '{}' (the normal state during an approval) a concurrent publish of seq N+1 matches nothing, takes no lock and does not serialize with the approval, which then commits {store: N}. AUDIT-2 GAP-G5-3 recorded this; P08's I48(1) work added the client-side embedded revisions (P08-CONTRACT.md:294) but left this function unchanged.
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner publishes a policy and clicks «اعتماد السياسات» within the same second (or publish_due commits a scheduled policy during the approval). Outcome: the approved set names a seq that is no longer live; after the next build every checkout sends the live seq and is refused POLICY_CHANGED, the quote still says checkoutEnabled: true, and no `commerce.policies_reset` audit row or admin signal explains why until the owner re-approves. Fail-closed (no order binds an unseen text), so low.
findings.proposed_fix: In commerce_policies_approve take the per-document advisory lock every policy writer already uses, before reading the seqs: `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:policies:' || d)) from unnest(array['store','delivery','refund','privacy']) d;` (or read each row `for share`), so a publish in flight either finishes first or waits for the approval and then resets it.

findings.title: Bidi override and isolate characters pass the buyer's name, address and dedication into the order snapshot, the admin and the mails
findings.evidence: checkout_create's contact check is `or v_name ~ '[[:cntrl:]]'` (line 471) and the address check `or v_address ~ '[[:cntrl:]]'` (line 520); finance.checkout_price refuses a dedication with the same class (line 119). Under a libc collation (Supabase default) PostgreSQL maps [[:cntrl:]] to iswcntrl, the Cc category (glibc adds U+2028/U+2029); only an ICU default collation would also take Cf. U+202A-U+202E (LRE/RLE/PDF/LRO/RLO), U+2066-U+2069 (isolates) and U+200B-U+200F/U+FEFF are Cf and pass. The function's rule is the same ASCII range: `noControlCharacters = (value) => !/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]/.test(value)` (supabase/functions/_shared/commerce-settings.ts:18). The snapshot columns customers.name / orders.customer_name, orders.address and order_items.dedication are shown in the admin order view (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:322), on the signed-edition checklist and in the receipt (order_email_data, 20261002120000_order_emails.sql:59).
findings.impact: A buyer (or a prankster using a known address) can type a name or delivery address containing U+202E so that the operations screen, the dedication checklist Anas writes from and the courier label the owner copies render it reversed or with digits reordered: a wrong dedication written into a signed copy, or a mis-copied address. Bounded to one order at a time, needs a hostile buyer, so low; the plan's own rule for untrusted text is 'Bidi isolation' (DATA-AND-SECURITY, last section), which isolates the surroundings but not the inside of the field.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the refusal to the formatting controls in both places: in SQL `~ '[[:cntrl:]‪-‮⁦-⁩]'` (PostgreSQL ARE character-entry escapes work inside a bracket) for v_name, v_address and v_dedication, and the same ranges in `noControlCharacters` so the field is named (the I48 (5) pattern). Leave ZWNJ/ZWJ/RLM (U+200C/U+200D/U+200F) alone: Arabic text uses them legitimately.
findings.proof_recipe: On the local stack: `select E'‮abc' ~ '[[:cntrl:]]';` expected false (the character passes); then call public.checkout_create with p_name = E'‮' || 'عبدالله' and a valid cart: expected ok:true and orders.customer_name containing U+202E. Also `show lc_ctype;` to record the collation provider.

findings.title: Coupon uses and committed preorder units are counted across environments, so the hosted sandbox runs permanently spend live coupon limits and preorder capacity
findings.evidence: finance.coupon_uses counts `finance.coupon_redemptions c where c.coupon_id = p_coupon_id and (c.state = 'committed' or ...)` with no join to the order's environment (lines 451-454); finance.preorder_committed likewise sums committed preorder reservations of any order (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:445-447), and variant_admin_info.preorderUnits (20261003110000:45-55) too. orders.environment and payment_attempts.environment exist, and the contract keeps test and live apart everywhere else (statistics, payment_view, order_access all take p_mode). A paid test order is never purged (order_erasable needs expired/cancelled) and a refund releases preorder reservations but never a coupon redemption (stats_disputes.sql:200-206), so once the hosted site runs the supervised sandbox (payments-runbook 'When the Moyasar keys arrive') with a coupon or a preorder, those uses stay counted after PAYMENTS_MODE flips to live. The 'Before live' list (payments-runbook.md:314) says to read the stock and says nothing of coupon uses or capacity.
findings.impact: Precondition: the sandbox pass on the hosted project (planned before launch) pays test orders that use the launch coupon or a preorder variant. On the live site the coupon reports COUPON_EXHAUSTED N uses early and the preorder offers N fewer units, and the variant form tells Anas to net N phantom confirmed preorders out of his real stock. Bounded to the number of test orders and correctable by hand (a higher usage_limit, SQL), so low; still a launch-day surprise with no admin control to undo it.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the counts mode-aware: give finance.coupon_uses and finance.preorder_committed (and finance.active_holds) a p_environment parameter and join finance.orders o on o.id = r.order_id and o.environment = p_environment; pass checkout_create's p_environment (and the order's own environment in order_try_commit) through finance.checkout_price / finance.availability, and let checkout_quote take p_environment from the function's config. Until then add to 'Before live': cancel or refund every test order, then release its redemptions and reservations by SQL as the migration role.

plan_gaps.title: The policy approval does not require a privacy policy, so an order can bind only store, delivery and refund revisions while a privacy policy is live or arrives later
plan_gaps.why_needed: commerce_policies_approve raises only when store, delivery or refund is unpublished (audit2_fixes.sql:116-118); privacy is folded in only if published at that moment, and DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:16 says a privacy policy published after the approval does not reset it. Every order snapshots policy_revisions, so orders made in that state carry no privacy revision; the buyer consented to a set that omits the privacy notice. Whether the store may sell without a privacy revision in the consent is Anas's and the legal gate's call (E08, PDPL notice at collection), not the code's.
plan_gaps.touches: public.commerce_policies_approve (require 'privacy' too, or record the decision), PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:16, docs/operations.md policy approval steps, I43

plan_gaps.title: The runbook's 'switch the preorder off when the copies arrive' step needs a precondition: no unpaid preorder hold and no paid_needs_resolution preorder order for that variant
plan_gaps.why_needed: docs/operations.md:1083-1089 tells the owner to switch preorder off and net the stock, but finance.order_try_commit decides by the reservation's own preorder flag against a capacity the form has just nulled (DB-COMMERCE-01), so a hold or an unresolved order caught by the switch can never be delivered through the admin. Until the code fix lands, the runbook must say: wait for the variant's held preorder reservations to reach zero (the form shows only confirmed, unshipped units today) and resolve every paid_needs_resolution order of the variant first; after the fix the step can stay as written.
plan_gaps.touches: docs/operations.md Preorders section, src/admin/tables/variants.ts (show held and unresolved preorder units beside the confirmed count), PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md section 4 availability rule

plan_gaps.title: No per-customer coupon limit exists anywhere in the plan or the schema
plan_gaps.why_needed: coupons carry usage_limit (store-wide), dates, minimum and product scope only (catalog_and_checkout.sql:153-174); finance.coupon_uses counts redemptions per coupon. A 'one per customer' launch code (the usual welcome discount) cannot be configured: the same address can redeem it once per order until the store-wide limit. Whether Anas wants such coupons decides if a per-email count (orders.email_hash join coupon_redemptions) is added to checkout_price.
plan_gaps.touches: public.coupons (a per_customer_limit column), finance.checkout_price coupon branch, src/admin/tables/coupons.ts, DATA-AND-SECURITY.md coupons row

doc_claims_checked.claim: The gateway refuses an invoice under 100 halalas (TOTAL_BELOW_MINIMUM, minimum 100 in finance.checkout_price and payment_attempt_begin)
doc_claims_checked.evidence: Create Invoice: amount is 'A positive integer representing the payment amount in the smallest currency unit', 'Possible values: >= 100'.

doc_claims_checked.claim: An invoice whose expired_at has passed cannot be paid, so the hold expiry (copied into the invoice's expired_at by startPayment) bounds late payments to those initiated before expiry
doc_claims_checked.evidence: expired_at: ISO 8601 date or datetime, default null; 'User will be prevented from paying the invoice once expired'; a date-only value sets the time to 00:00:00.

doc_claims_checked.claim: `perform 1 from public.product_variants v where v.id = any(v_ids) order by v.id for update` acquires the row locks in ascending id, so checkout_create, order_try_commit, refund_lock_rows and return_receive share one lock order on variants
doc_claims_checked.evidence: 'ORDER BY is applied first. The command sorts the result, but might then block trying to obtain a lock on one or more of the rows.' Locks are taken in the sorted order; rows that satisfied the conditions as of the snapshot are locked even when no longer returned.
